findings.F1: The tested measure lands on the predicted side but short of the bar: slope t 1.47 on 8,650 grid points over 1,509 days; the unusual move is only +0.09 % per case (t 0.53, 1,681 days), a strength of 0.014, while one trade costs 0.19 %.
findings.F2: The volatility half of the idea points the wrong way. Among 2-day falls, those in each coin's low-volatility half earn a mean excess of +0.19 % with a fall-size t of 1.98. Those in the high-volatility half earn -0.07 % with t 1.05. Step 5's own high-minus-low difference is also negative, -0.08 %.
findings.F3: The fall measured in units of the coin's 60-day volatility predicts the rebound better than the fall times volatility. On fall days over 2 days, its t is 2.01 against 0.93 for fall × volatility. On all grid points its t is 1.68 against 0.91.
findings.F4: The rebound grows steadily with the volatility-scaled fall. By quintile of fall/volatility on 2-day fall cases (about 560 each), the mean excess return is -0.36 %, -0.54 %, -0.03 %, +0.51 % and +0.71 %. The top quintile's unusual move is about 3.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and the top quartile's strength is 0.083.
findings.F5: The effect is mixed across coins. With the volatility-scaled fall over 2 days, XMR shows t 2.17, XRP 2.11, LTC 1.57 and ZEC 1.43, against BTC -0.14 and ETH 0.11. Every year from 2019 to 2025 has a positive t (0.07 to 1.50); 2018 alone is at -0.10.
findings.F6: The rebound shows most at the shortest horizon. On all grid points, the raw fall has a t of 2.79 over 1 day (11,620 points, 1,938 days), 1.38 over 2 days and 1.87 over 3 days. By 5 days it has faded: on fall days its t is 0.37 there.
findings.F7: Up days do not mirror this: a rise scaled by volatility gives a t of 0.59 on the next 2 days' excess return, so the effect is on the falling side only.

ideas.name: volatile falls, more coins
ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 2 days, and this rebound is larger the higher the coin's volatility over the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying the dip should expect the largest short rebounds after big falls in turbulent periods and little after falls in calm ones, which makes the bet worth its cost mainly when volatility is high.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, measured against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: A dip buyer should size the bet by how unusual the fall is for the coin's recent volatility, not by how volatile the coin has been, since only the falls that are most unusual for the coin pay well beyond the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: unusually large falls rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, measured against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying the dip should expect most of the rebound on the very next day and hold the position briefly.
ideas.name: next-day rebound after falls
